method: Parsed the captured module registries in all 144 JavaScript bundles. Module keys were retained in private memory only to join literal module-import calls, then discarded. Public output uses archive-local bundle and 1-based module ordinals.
uses: The resolved imports corroborate separately reviewed source-level render, keyboard landmark and history-loading relationships.
The complete capture helps distinguish external or missing module references from references uniquely identifiable within the archived bundles.
These relationships can seed follow-up caller and component tracing for future dumps without publishing minified module names.
limits: Static require calls are candidate dependency edges; runtime chunk loading or invocation was not observed.
An unresolved candidate need not be broken: it may reference a separately loaded module or a dynamic mechanism outside the capture.
A duplicated module key is deliberately ambiguous; its import edges were not assigned speculative targets.
Counted import candidates are unique literal module references per factory, not the number of calls executed.
The source bundles are a single archived snapshot and do not establish current deployed client behavior.
privacy: Only anonymous source ordinals, module ordinals, structural counts and authored roles are published; original identifiers, source file names, URLs, code, payloads and account data remain private.
